members: Haloperidol - High-potency Butyrophenone, high D2 affinity, low sedation (Dulcan p.787, StahlNeuro p.180, StahlKids p.254)
Chlorpromazine - Low-potency Phenothiazine, high sedation, M1, alpha-1 blockade (Dulcan p.787, StahlNeuro p.180, StahlKids p.96)
Fluphenazine - High-potency Phenothiazine, high EPS, available as decanoate LAI (Dulcan p.787, StahlKids p.213)
Pimozide - High-potency Diphenylbutylpiperidine, D2 + calcium channel blocker, unique to Tourette (Dulcan p.447, StahlKids p.395)
drug_class.mechanism: Dopamine D2 receptor antagonism across mesolimbic, nigrostriatal, tuberoinfundibular, and mesocortical pathways (Dulcan p.794, StahlNeuro p.161)
kinetics: Half-life oral Haloperidol: ~18 hours (Dulcan p.788, StahlKids p.255)
Metabolism: Hepatic via CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 (Dulcan p.786, StahlKids p.255)
Plasma drug levels: Measurable for Haloperidol (StahlKids p.255, StahlNeuro p.202)
drug_class.onset_of_effect: Acute sedation/antipsychotic action in hours to days; full antipsychotic effect in 2–6 weeks (Dulcan p.795, StahlNeuro p.161)

items: Schizophrenia in youth: Haloperidol approved >=3 years, Trifluoperazine approved >=6 years, Thiothixene approved >=12 years (Dulcan p.402, p.796)
Tourette Syndrome: Haloperidol (FDA approved), Pimozide approved >=8 years as 2nd line (Dulcan p.447, StahlKids p.395)
Severe behavior problems & ADHD: Legacy FDA approval for Chlorpromazine and Haloperidol (StahlKids p.96, p.254)
key_numbers: 60-70% - D2 occupancy required for antipsychotic effect (Dulcan p.795, StahlNeuro p.161)
3 years - Minimum approved age for Haloperidol in schizophrenia (Dulcan p.402)
8 years - Minimum approved age for Pimozide in Tourette (Dulcan p.447, StahlKids p.395)

items: Hyperprolactinemia: Galactorrhea, amenorrhea, gynecomastia via tuberoinfundibular D2 blockade (Dulcan p.820, StahlNeuro p.164)
Sedation: H1 and M1 blockade, prominent in low-potency FGAs like Chlorpromazine (StahlNeuro p.180, StahlKids p.97)
Anticholinergic effects: Dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention via M1 blockade (StahlNeuro p.168)
QTc prolongation: Risk of Torsades de Pointes, especially with Pimozide and Thioridazine (Dulcan p.447, StahlKids p.396)
key_numbers: >80% - D2 occupancy threshold causing EPS and hyperprolactinemia (Dulcan p.795, StahlNeuro p.161)
10-20% - Fatality rate of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) (DSM p.810)

items: AIMS scale: Mandatory baseline and periodic screening for Tardive Dyskinesia (Dulcan p.827)
ECG and electrolytes: Required at baseline and titration for Pimozide (Dulcan p.447, StahlKids p.396)
CYP2D6 genotyping: Required before exceeding 0.05 mg/kg/day of Pimozide (StahlKids p.400)
Metabolic & vital monitoring: Weight, BMI z-score, BP, fasting glucose/lipids (Dulcan p.827)
key_numbers: 0.05 mg/kg/day - Pimozide dose threshold requiring CYP2D6 genotyping (StahlKids p.400)
3 months - Interval for initial post-baseline AIMS and metabolic re-evaluation (Dulcan p.827)

items: Start low, go slow: Weight-based dosing and slow titration due to pediatric sensitivity (Dulcan p.686, StahlKids p.39)
LAI formulations: Haldol decanoate and Fluphenazine decanoate not FDA-approved in youth; contra-indicated <12 years (Dulcan p.402, StahlKids p.218)
Chemical straightjacket prohibition: Strict ethical ban on using FGAs for non-specific behavioral control without diagnosis (StahlKids p.104, Dulcan p.508)
key_numbers: 10 mg/day - Absolute maximum daily dose of Pimozide (Dulcan p.448, StahlKids p.400)
12 years - Minimum age for Fluphenazine decanoate (StahlKids p.218)

items: Acute Dystonia: Sustained muscle contraction (torticollis, oculogyric crisis, laryngeal dystonia); treat with IM/IV Benztropine (DSM p.812)
Parkinsonism (DIP): Rigidity, bradykinesia, 3-6 Hz rest tremor; treat with dose reduction or oral anticholinergics (DSM p.807, StahlNeuro p.165)
Acute Akathisia: Subjective inner restlessness + objective pacing; treat with Propranolol (DSM p.813, StahlNeuro p.169)

Tardive Dyskinesia (TD): Orofacial dyskinesia from upregulated/supersensitive D2 receptors; treat with VMAT2 inhibitors (Valbenazine/Deutetrabenazine); anticholinergics worsen TD! (DSM p.814, StahlNeuro p.170)
NMS: Hyperthermia (>38°C), lead-pipe rigidity, autonomic instability, CPK elevation; treat with withdrawal, ICU, Dantrolene/Bromocriptine (DSM p.810)
key_numbers: 24-48 hours - Timeframe for 50% of Acute Dystonia onset (DSM p.812)
3-6 Hz - Frequency of parkinsonian resting tremor (DSM p.808)
3 months - Minimum exposure duration before diagnosing Tardive Dyskinesia (DSM p.815)

items: High-potency (Haloperidol, Fluphenazine): High D2 affinity, low mg dose, high EPS, low sedation/anticholinergic (Dulcan p.787, StahlNeuro p.180)
Low-potency (Chlorpromazine): Low D2 affinity, high mg dose, low EPS, high sedation/anticholinergic/orthostasis (Dulcan p.787, StahlNeuro p.180)
Chlorpromazine equivalence: 2 mg Haloperidol = 2 mg Fluphenazine = 2 mg Pimozide = 100 mg Chlorpromazine (Dulcan p.787)
key_numbers: 100 mg - Standard Chlorpromazine dose equivalent baseline (Dulcan p.787)
2 mg - Equivalent dose of Haloperidol to 100 mg Chlorpromazine (Dulcan p.787)

high_yield: Anticholinergics treat DIP but WORSEN Tardive Dyskinesia (TD) (DSM p.815, StahlNeuro p.170)
Propranolol is the first-line treatment for acute akathisia, not anticholinergics (DSM p.813, StahlNeuro p.169)
Pimozide requires baseline ECG, electrolyte check, and CYP2D6 genotyping due to QTc risk (Dulcan p.447, StahlKids p.400)
Acute laryngeal dystonia is a life-threatening airway emergency treated immediately with IM/IV Benztropine or Diphenhydramine (DSM p.812)
TEOSS study showed equal efficacy between Molindone (FGA) and SGAs in early-onset schizophrenia, but higher EPS (Dulcan p.402, p.821)
VMAT2 inhibitors (Valbenazine, Deutetrabenazine) are FDA-approved treatments for Tardive Dyskinesia (DSM p.816, StahlNeuro p.173)
